### 1 — Scene
A dinner plate with white rice, browned chicken pieces, broccoli, and roasted potato wedges.

### 2 — Vessel
A large square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Allowing for its square shape and rounded corners, I’ll use an effective circular diameter of **27 cm**:
**Area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm².**

### 3 — Items
White rice; browned, possibly lightly coated chicken; broccoli; skin-on potato wedges. There is a light oily sheen, included in the cooked-food energy estimates rather than counted separately.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
The estimated footprints total **75% of the plate**, leaving about 25% exposed.

| Item | Plate area | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| White rice | 24% | 137 cm² × 1.9 cm = 261 ml | 0.8 | 209 g | 130 | 272 kcal |
| Chicken pieces | 17% | 97 cm² × 1.3 cm = 126 ml | 1.0 | 126 g | 220 | 277 kcal |
| Broccoli | 16% | 92 cm² × 2.0 cm = 183 ml | 0.6 | 110 g | 45 | 50 kcal |
| Roasted potato wedges | 18% | 103 cm² × 1.7 cm = 175 ml | 0.65 | 114 g | 180 | 205 kcal |

### 8 — Sanity check
**About 559 g and 804 kcal** is plausible for this substantially covered dinner plate. The main uncertainties are the chicken’s coating and the amount of cooking oil; a reasonable energy range is roughly **650–950 kcal**.
